name: Public opera at Venice’s San Cassiano
description: A professional opera company performed staged drama in music for a paying public at Venice’s San Cassiano theatre.

date.label: early 1637
date.basis: The cited source dates this historical episode.

events.statement: A touring company performed Manelli’s Andromeda at San Cassiano for a paying Venetian audience.

evidence.supports: Describes an early-1637 production of Manelli’s Andromeda at San Cassiano by six singers and instrumentalists for a broad Venetian audience.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest event established in the sources collected here; not a claim of global priority.

caveats: Opera and public performance preceded this episode. A paying audience was broader than court-only access but did not make the theatre accessible to every Venetian. Glover describes six singers, while Rosand finds seven named in the libretto; the cast count remains unsettled. The libretto’s account of self-financing is reported by Rosand alongside evidence of some noble support; it should not be read as excluding all patrons.
